doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Overseas tour and being treated as an artist
summary: He stays on for the European tour, is praised in programs and treated with respect, in contrast to home.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What was it like going overseas with the group?
Well after I told Mercer, I says well I don’t care for this, I think I’ll go back to Philly. It’s not what I thought it was.
How long were you in the band?

Oh two or three months. Or maybe a month or so. I said I don’t care for this. Well Mercer says, “why don’t you go overseas first, then make your decision.” He says, “we’re going over around January or February or something like that.” So okay, I hung in there and we went overseas. And I discovered that the audiences were much different. That made an impression. They were quite receptive to Duke’s band. And I noticed that when I went to England, there I was, my picture was in the program, not a picture but a statement. They say “this young man reminds us of the great Jimmy Blanton in his sound.” I said hmmm. Looks good. And then at another place in France they had my picture on the front page. We were artists. We weren’t somebody just playing a instrument. And the people showed it. There was one fellow that I met that asked to carry my bass who was a cabby, asked if he would take it to the concert hall. He took the instrument, put it on top of his cab, tied it down, he called me sir. An entirely different thing then I had experienced over here earlier you know. And I hopped in. He closed the door, walked in, and I gave him a nice tip I hope, because it was foreign exchange. And the people were always so, so warm and receptive. I guess that’s what it meant at that time to be a celebrity or with Duke Ellington. Then when we got back over here I took a bus, a city bus, with the bass, hopped on the bus and the driver says, “where are you going with that thing?” Well I’m going to the city you know. But I’m showing a difference in the attitude.
Yeah. Welcome home. © Fillius Jazz Archive -25-

Yeah. We were well received there. We were received over here by fans, all the fans of Duke loved Duke. But those that didn’t understand the music or didn’t have anything to do with it, we were just, you know, in my opinion.
